# Harmony Biosciences Announces Planned CEO Transition to Support Next Phase of Growth

October 12, 2026 | 9 min read

The Board of Directors has appointed Peter Anastasiou, former Harmony board member and current Sr. EVP and COO, to become President, Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board, effective January 1, 2027.

Current CEO Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire at the end of the year following a nine-year tenure at the Company, including as Chief Medical Officer, and step down as a member of the Board.

The Company reiterates full-year 2026 WAKIX® net revenue guidance of $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion, remains on track to report data from the multiple ascending dose (MAD) study of BP-205 in Q4 2026, and is focused on executing its previously communicated strategic priorities.

PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: HRMY) (“Harmony” or the “Company”) today announced that, as part of the Board of Directors’ succession planning, Peter Anastasiou, former Harmony board member and current Sr. EVP and Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed President, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board of Directors, effective January 1, 2027. He succeeds Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., who will retire as President and CEO and step down from the Board of Directors on December 31, 2026. To support the leadership transition, Dr. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor to the Company throughout 2027 to support Harmony’s growth objectives.

The planned succession comes as Harmony enters its next phase of growth from a position of financial and operational strength. The Company remains focused on its strategic priorities: growing the pitolisant franchise; advancing its diversified CNS pipeline, led by potential best-in-class orexin agonist BP-205; deploying capital strategically by transacting on value-creating assets; and protecting WAKIX® exclusivity.

“Jeff has led Harmony through a period of strong growth, establishing WAKIX as a leading treatment in narcolepsy, advancing the pitolisant lifecycle management strategy, diversifying the pipeline for sustained long-term growth and leaving the Company in a position of financial strength,” said Jeffrey S. Aronin, founder and Chairman of the Board of Harmony. “The Board is grateful for Jeff’s leadership and his commitment to patients, employees and shareholders.”

“Peter is the right leader for Harmony’s next phase of growth. He has a deep understanding of our business and has been an important contributor to our strategy, pipeline and business development efforts,” continued Aronin. “Peter also brings more than three decades of biopharmaceutical experience, leading organizations in commercializing, acquiring and developing treatments for both broad and rare CNS diseases to serve patients and create value for shareholders.”

“It has been a privilege to lead Harmony through a phase of significant growth, and I am grateful to the Board for the opportunity to have served as CEO. It has also been my honor to work alongside such a talented team of individuals who are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients with unmet needs,” said Dayno. “Peter knows Harmony’s business exceptionally well, I have great confidence in his leadership, and I look forward to supporting him, the Board and the Company through this transition.”

“I am honored to serve as Harmony’s next CEO and am grateful to the Board for this opportunity. # Harmony Biosciences names Peter Anastasiou as next CEO

Published Oct 12, 2026, 07:04 AM

PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa. - Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:HRMY) announced Monday that Peter Anastasiou will become President and Chief Executive Officer effective January 1, 2027, according to a press release statement.

Anastasiou, currently serving as Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, will succeed Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., who will retire as President and CEO on December 31, 2026, after nine years with the company. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor throughout 2027.

Anastasiou previously served on Harmony’s Board of Directors for three years before joining as COO. He was Chief Executive Officer of Capsida Biotherapeutics for nearly four years, where he raised more than $165 million in capital and secured partnerships with AbbVie and Lilly. Prior to that, he served as Executive Vice President and President of North America at Lundbeck, leading an organization of approximately 1,200 employees with annual net revenues exceeding $1.5 billion.

The company reiterated its full-year 2026 WAKIX net revenue guidance of $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion. Harmony stated it remains on track to report data from the multiple ascending dose study of BP-205 in the fourth quarter of 2026.

"Peter is the right leader for Harmony’s next phase of growth," said Jeffrey S. Aronin, founder and Chairman of the Board. "He has a deep understanding of our business and has been an important contributor to our strategy, pipeline and business development efforts."

Harmony stated it remains focused on growing the pitolisant franchise, advancing its CNS pipeline, deploying capital strategically, and protecting WAKIX exclusivity. The company does not currently expect changes in the timing of key commercial and pipeline milestones.

Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 13, 2026, reporting that President and Chief Executive Officer Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire effective December 31, 2026, and that Chief Operating Officer Peter Anastasiou has been appointed to succeed him as President and CEO beginning January 1, 2027.

### Key Highlights

- CEO retirement: Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire as President and CEO and step down as a Class I director, effective December 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.
- Successor named: Peter Anastasiou, the Company's current Chief Operating Officer, will become President and CEO effective January 1, 2027, at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time.
- Board appointment: The Board also appointed Mr. Anastasiou as a Class I director effective January 1, 2027, with a term expiring at the Company's 2027 Annual Meeting of Stockholders.
- Advisory role: Dr. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor to the Company through 2027.
- Prior experience: Mr. Anastasiou, age 55, has served as the Company's Chief Operating Officer since April 2026, and previously served as CEO of Capsida Biotherapeutics from January 2022 to October 2025.
- No additional director compensation: According to the filing, Mr. Anastasiou will not receive any additional compensation for his service as a director.

## Leadership Transition Details at Harmony Biosciences

According to the filing, the leadership change is described as part of "a leadership succession plan." Dr. Dayno's retirement as President, CEO, and Class I director takes effect December 31, 2026, after which he will transition to a non-executive advisory role through 2027. The Company, traded on NASDAQ:HRMY, made the announcement on October 12, 2026.

The filing states that the Board appointed Peter Anastasiou, currently serving as Chief Operating Officer, to fill the CEO role starting January 1, 2027. Mr. Anastasiou, age 55, joined the Company as Chief Operating Officer in April 2026. Before that, he served as CEO and board member of Capsida Biotherapeutics from January 2022 to October 2025. From November 2009 to December 2021, according to the filing, he held multiple roles at Lundbeck, including Executive Vice President and President of North America and Chief Commercial Officer for the U.S. The filing notes that Lundbeck is "a pharmaceutical company publicly traded on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange."

The filing further discloses that Mr. Anastasiou previously served as a member of the Company's Board from November 2023 to April 2026. He holds a B.A. in Economics and Management from Albion College and an M.B.A. from the Kelley School of Business, Indiana University. The filing states there are no arrangements or understandings between Mr. Anastasiou and any other person regarding his selection, no family relationships with any director or executive officer, and no transactions requiring disclosure under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.

## What Was Disclosed

The 8-K disclosed a CEO succession plan at Harmony Biosciences: Jeffrey Dayno will retire on December 31, 2026, and Peter Anastasiou, current COO, will assume the President and CEO role and a Class I board seat on January 1, 2027.

Harmony Biosciences CEO Jeffrey Dayno to Retire December 31, 2026 - The Pharma Vanguard

# Harmony Biosciences CEO Jeffrey Dayno to Retire December 31, 2026

October 14, 2026

By Jon Napitupulu

 

Harmony Biosciences has a leadership gap opening at the top: Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., the company’s President, CEO, and board director, will retire effective December 31, 2026, leaving a narcolepsy-focused company with $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion in projected 2026 WAKIX revenue in need of a permanent chief executive heading into what looks like a critical commercial year.

Dayno will stay on as a non-executive advisor through 2027 to smooth the handoff, but the timing deserves scrutiny. WAKIX net revenue guidance sits at a billion-dollar threshold that the company has worked years to reach, and the stock was already trading well below even the low end of analyst price targets when the October 12 filing dropped. A CEO transition at that inflection point raises real questions about whether the exit is entirely planned or whether board-level pressure played a role, though the filing does not say either way.

Harmony’s entire commercial story runs through WAKIX (pitolisant), which earned FDA approval for excessive daytime sleepiness in adult narcolepsy patients in 2019 and built a market position in a space where oxybate formulations from Jazz Pharmaceuticals also compete. Whoever steps into the CEO seat inherits both the revenue momentum and the competitive pressure, with no diversified pipeline to absorb a stumble. Peter Anastasiou, currently Senior Executive Vice President, was named in the announcement materials as part of the transition context, per the company’s public disclosure, though the 8-K stops short of naming a permanent successor.

The name that fills the permanent CEO slot will tell investors whether Harmony is building toward a broader CNS platform or positioning the company for a sale while WAKIX revenue is at its peak.
